thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: /v1/generate 95th latency spike detected (>1200ms) across prod-us-east1, rate 120rps. Alert: kv_cache_evictions rising. Pager severity: page_all_oncall.
charlie (oncall): I'm on it. pinging alice for SRE context. any quick impact numbers?
alice (SRE): seeing tail latencies spike around 21:06 UTC. KV eviction rate jumped, some hosts showing OOM+evictions. Not seeing obvious full node failures yet.
charlie (oncall): ops-bot, can you attach recent host metrics?
ops-bot: Attached graphs: host-kv-01 eviction_rate 0.9 -> 7.2 (per min), cpu 78% -> 96%, net I/O steady.
bob (Runtime): likely caused by recent rollout of batching tweak on the runtime (small change yesterday). If KV cache size assumptions changed we could be causing thrash under bursty workloads.
charlie (oncall): Maria, any customer-side reports?
maria (Support): A handful of customers reported increased request timeouts starting ~20:58 UTC. Tracking two enterprise customers with high QPS. No data exfiltration.
dana (Product): putting a heads-up on status page? We should be careful, scope is partial.
charlie (oncall): Agreed. For live mitigations: 1) revert the runtime batching tweak to previous config on the smallest canary ring, 2) temporarily reduce max batch size to limit memory usage, 3) increase KV cache admission threshold to reduce evictions. I'll run 1 and 2. Alice/Triage please coordinate 3.
alice (SRE): I'm SSHing to the cluster. Running quick grep for eviction logs:
```
grep -R "eviction" /var/log/inference | tail -n 50
[kv-client] evicted key=hot:request:abcd ttl=0 host=host-kv-01
[kv-client] eviction_count=672 host=host-kv-01
```
charlie (oncall): Rolling batch config rollback now: `deploy rollback --service runtime --to-tag runtime-2026-03-10`
ops-bot: Rollback started on 10 hosts in prod-us-east1.
charlie (oncall): Reducing max_batch_size to 32 on prod-us-east1: `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/runtime MAX_BATCH=32 --record`
bob (Runtime): Good. That should reduce per-request memory pressure. I'm standing by to revert if errors follow.
alice (SRE): Increasing KV cache admission threshold from 0.6 -> 0.8 on kv-client config and restarting kv-proxy on affected nodes. Config snippet:
```
kv_admit_threshold: 0.8
kv_max_entries: 500000
```
alice (SRE): Restarted kv-proxy on host-kv-01..05. Evictions dropping on those hosts. Monitoring overall.
maria (Support): Customer A saw errors drop after ~5m. Replied to their ticket with status update.
dana (Product): I'll hold off status page update until we confirm stability.
charlie (oncall): Observability: 95th latency back down to ~220ms after rollback and KV tweak. Still elevated vs baseline but trending OK.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> requiring post-incident review. Please nominate DRI and fill postmortem checklist.
charlie (oncall): DRI: alice (SRE) for root cause + remediation. Postmortem draft requested by EOD tomorrow.
alice (SRE): I'll own RCA. Initial hypothesis: recent runtime batching change increased transient memory pressure under burst patterns which amplified KV cache churn; combined with conservative KV admission threshold led to eviction storms.
bob (Runtime): Follow-ups for runtime: 1) revert batching param permanently until we have safe rollback tests, 2) add canary-wide synthetic load tests for bursty traffic, 3) add feature flag to gate the new batching behavior so it can be toggled without deploy. Owner: @bob.
charlie (oncall): Runbook/playbook updates needed: - add explicit step to revert batching changes and fallback to previous batch policy, - include KV cache eviction indicators as a paging signal (eviction_rate > 2/min triggers oncall), - document the ad-hoc command lines we used. Owner: @charlie + @alice.
dana (Product): Add customer communication play to on-call playbook: quick template for Support to send when timeouts/latency occur and mitigation underway. Owner: @dana.
maria (Support): I'll draft the template and link to the ticket.
alice (SRE): Action items list (we'll track in the postmortem):
1) Runtime: gate batching change behind feature flag + unit/canary tests. Owner: bob. Due: 2026-03-20.
2) KV: review and lower default admission_threshold; add alert for eviction_rate and a histogram for eviction bursts. Owner: alice. Due: 2026-03-18.
3) Playbook: add dedicated step for immediate rollback + explicit commands used. Owner: charlie. Due: 2026-03-17.
4) Support comms template and status page rules. Owner: maria/dana. Due: 2026-03-16.
5) Postmortem write-up + RCA + timeline. Owner: alice. Due: 2026-03-16 EOD.
charlie (oncall): Scheduling: postmortem meeting Thursday 09:30 UTC. Invitees: SRE, Runtime, Product, Support. I'll create calendar invite.
dana (Product): please include account reps for the two affected customers so they get notified of RCA.
alice (SRE): I'll paste initial timeline into the doc and link logs/metrics.
bob (Runtime): Also adding an integration test that simulates TTL eviction under bursty QPS; will open PR with test skeleton.
charlie (oncall): Quick runbook patch (to be merged after postmortem) — adding snippet below for immediate use:
```
If high_95th_latency AND kv_eviction_rate > 2/min:
  - rollback runtime batching: deploy rollback --service runtime --to-tag <last-stable>
  - reduce MAX_BATCH to 32
  - increase kv_admit_threshold temporarily to 0.8 and restart kv-proxy on hot nodes
  - notify Support for customer-facing comms
```
charlie (oncall): tagging owners in the doc and moving this thread to the postmortem doc. If anyone has objections to the timelines or owners, speak up now.
maria (Support): LGTM. I'll coordinate the customer follow-ups after postmortem.
dana (Product): LGTM. Thanks all for fast response.
alice (SRE): Closing the pager. I'll update the postmortem doc with logs and the RCA draft.
incident-bot: Incident marked: resolved -> postmortem scheduled. Reminder: link the runbook PR to the postmortem when opened.
charlie (oncall): nice teamwork :thumbsup: we'll iterate on the playbook to avoid surprises next time.
